title: Behold, the $3,000 keyboard that is also actually a powerful AI PC I would hate to spill my coffee on
key_facts: HP's EliteBoard series, a keyboard with a whole PC inside, debuted with the G1a at CES 2026; the G2a is the refresh.
HP pitches the EliteBoard G2a as a 'Next Gen AI PC' and it has a Copilot key.
It has up to 32 GB of RAM and an AMD Gorgon Point CPU.
Pricing starts at $3,028 for the most basic US model (16 GB RAM, Ryzen AI 5 Pro 435).
The top model has a Ryzen AI 7 Pro 450 and 32 GB of RAM, weighs under 700 grams (the G1a weighed 780 grams) and costs $4,191.
It plugs only into a monitor with a USB-C connection; the USB4 cable is fixed, and the model with a detachable cable starts at $3,053.
The writer says $3,000 is a lot even for a prebuilt gaming PC and that she would hate to spill coffee on it.
quote_evidence: Pricing starts at $3,028, with the most ‘basic’ model available in the US featuring 16 GB of RAM and an AMD Ryzen AI 5 Pro 435 processor.
It will set you back an eye-watering $4,191, though.
why_it_matters_hint: An AI-branded keyboard PC at laptop-plus prices; the writer doubts the price and design.
notes: Full text read. Specs and prices from one outlet; no independent testing in the piece. The coffee-spill and price remarks are the writer's opinion.
